units.text: With it anoint the Tent of Testimony and the ark of the testimony,
the lampstand and all its utensils, and the incense altar,
the altar of whole burnt offerings and all its utensils, the table and all its utensils, and the basin and its base.
Consecrate them, and they shall be most holy. Everyone who touches them shall be sanctified.
And the Lord said to Moses, “Go in to Pharaoh, and you shall say to him, ‘Thus says the Lord, the God of the Hebrews: Let My people go, that they may serve Me.
But if you will not let My people go, and still hold them,

behold, the hand of the Lord shall be upon your livestock in the plains, upon the horses, and upon the beasts of burden, and upon the camels, and upon the cattle, and upon the sheep: an exceedingly great death.
At that time I will make a marvellous distinction between the Egyptians’ livestock and the sons of Israel’s livestock. Nothing belonging to the sons of Israel shall die.’”
God appointed a time, saying, “Tomorrow the Lord will do this in the land.”
The Lord did this the next day. All the Egyptians’ livestock died, but none of the sons of Israel’s livestock died.
Pharaoh saw that none of the sons of Israel’s livestock had died. Yet Pharaoh’s heart became heavy, and he did not let the people go.
On that day there will be an altar to the Lord in the Egyptians’ country and a pillar to the Lord by its border,

and it will be an everlasting sign to the Lord in Egypt’s country, because they will cry to the Lord on account of their oppressors. The Lord will send them a man who will save them; judging, he will save them.
The Lord will be known to the Egyptians, and the Egyptians will know the Lord on that day. They will make sacrifices, vow vows to the Lord and pay them.
The Lord will strike the Egyptians with a great blow and heal them with healing. They will turn back to the Lord, and He will listen to them and heal them.
On that day there will be a road from Egypt toward the Assyrians. Assyrians will enter Egypt, and Egyptians go toward the Assyrians, and the Egyptians will serve the Assyrians.
On that day Israel will be third among the Assyrians and Egyptians, blessed upon the earth,
which the Lord Sabaoth blessed, saying, “Blessed be My people in Egypt and among the Assyrians, and My inheritance Israel.”
Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and a city will be built for the Lord from Hanamel’s tower to the Corner Gate.
And its measurement will go out opposite them as far as Gareb’s hills, and it will be enclosed all around with chosen stones.
And all Asaremoth as far as the Kidron wadi, to the corner of the eastern Horse Gate, will be a sanctuary for the Lord. It will certainly never disappear or be torn down for ever.
Because you trusted in your fortifications, you too will be seized. Chemosh will go into deportation, his priests and rulers together.

Shout aloud, Heshbon, for Gai perished! Cry out, daughters of Rabbath; put on sackcloth, be seized with distress, and beat yourselves over Melchom, for he will go into deportation, his priests and rulers together.
Thus they will inherit the land a second time, and everlasting joy will be over their head.
“For I am the Lord who loves righteousness and hates plunder obtained through injustice. I will give their labor’s yield to righteous people and make an everlasting covenant with them.
Their offspring and descendants will be known among nations. Everyone seeing them will recognize them, because they are offspring blessed by God,
Into their bosom like earth, like an eagle against the Lord’s house, because they transgressed My covenant and acted impiously against My law.
They will cry to Me, ‘God, we know Thee!’
Because Israel turned away good things, they pursued an enemy.
But God chose the foolish things of the world to shame the wise, and God chose the weak things of the world to shame the strong;
and God chose the lowborn things of the world and the despised things, the things that are not, to bring to nothing the things that are,
so that no flesh may boast before God.
